The paper considers the problem of electromagnetic radiation and scattering from perfectly conducting bodies of revolution of arbitrary shape.
The mathematical formulation is an integro-differential equation obtained from the potential integrals and boundary conditions.
The solution is obtained using the method of moments, with the results expressed in terms of generalized network parameters.
A computer program was developed to compute the generalized impedance matrix for an arbitrary body of revolution.
The expansion functions chosen are harmonic in the azimuthal angle θ and subsectional in the contour length variable t.
Due to rotational symmetry, the problem reduces to a set of independent modes, one for each harmonic term.
Numerical results are presented for a conducting sphere and a cone-sphere body, comparing to analytical eigenfunction solutions where available.
For the sphere, the real part of the current density agreed well with the eigenfunction solution, but the imaginary part converged slowly.
Radiation patterns computed from the numerical and analytical solutions agreed to within a few percent.
The cone-sphere example illustrates the application of the general program to problems not solvable by classical methods.
The impedance elements, currents, radiation patterns, and scattering patterns were computed for the test cases.
The paper includes details on the numerical evaluation of the impedance matrix elements, including approximations used.
The computer program is written in Fortran IV and can compute one mode at a time for a body of revolution.
Input data includes the mode number, total length of the generating curve, number of subdivisions, wavenumber, and geometric parameters.
Output includes the Green's function terms, impedance matrix, admittance matrix, and other computed quantities.
